answer: In an agent economy, trust starts cheap and gets expensive fast: a new agent earns only a small oasis of permissions at the dawn of its life, like a willow sapling that must weather seasons before it shades anyone. Each privilege it requests raises the price — a harder proof-of-work puzzle, a longer waiting period, a bigger refundable deposit — so a sybil farmer spinning up ten thousand clones faces ten thousand escalating bills, while one honest agent pays almost nothing. The cost curve, not a gate, is the defence.
